slides.title: Petal length across three iris species
slides.subtitle: A short talk using 150 observations from the UCI Iris dataset.
slides.notes: Fisher, R. (1936). Iris [Dataset]. UCI Machine Learning Repository. https://doi.org/10.24432/C56C76. Dataset licensed CC BY 4.0. This deck uses the bezdekIris.data file and calculates descriptive summaries.

slides.title: Each plant contributes one petal-length measurement

steps.heading: Read the records
steps.text: Use the petal length in centimetres from all 150 rows.

steps.heading: Group by species
steps.text: Setosa, versicolor and virginica each contribute 50 plants.

steps.heading: Compare summaries
steps.text: Calculate a mean for each group, then inspect its observed range.

slides.source: R. Fisher · UCI Iris · bezdekIris.data, columns 3 and 5
slides.notes: The input is a frozen copy of the file in the UCI archive. summarize.py uses decimal arithmetic and keeps three decimal places for the means.

slides.title: Virginica petals average {{virginica}}
slides.notes: Each bar is the arithmetic mean for 50 observations. The title, labels and difference use the same three-decimal source table. Values on screen are rounded to two decimals.

slides.title: The observed ranges overlap for two species
slides.notes: Versicolor ranges from 3.0 to 5.1 cm and virginica from 4.5 to 6.9 cm. The intervals overlap even though the means differ.

slides.title: Mean petal length summarizes differences between groups
slides.takeaway: Versicolor and virginica share part of the observed range.
items: A classification study could add petal width and evaluate held-out plants.
slides.notes: The overlap refers to the intervals between the observed extrema. The classification study is a suggested next experiment.
